runtime_posture.control_transport: fixed-argv Docker CLI exec/copy through the local Docker daemon; the service has no host TCP or Unix-socket publication
runtime_posture.fixture_transfer: after runtime preflight only, each tracked fixture is opened once into an immutable manifest-verified byte buffer; fixed docker cp - receives a deterministic in-memory tar stream from those exact bytes; each archive entry is copied once and removed after its one index request, while the query buffer is copied and removed in two separate transfer/request pairs for the pre-index probe and post-index product query
runtime_posture.control_operation_seal: every docker cp and docker exec is bracketed by a normalized inspect projection; the projection binds image identity, command argv, labels, process user, host configuration, mounts, running state, start timestamp, restart count, network attachments, published ports, and integration environment; each copy also binds the transferred content SHA-256; drift fails before the next drawing-byte operation and ordered checkpoints are bound by runtime_seal_receipt_sha256
runtime_posture.outbound_probe: docker exec first requires curl --version to exit 0, then invokes curl --noproxy '*' --silent --show-error --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' --connect-timeout 2 --max-time 3 http://198.51.100.1:80/ inside the empty network-none container; probe must exit 7 with stdout exactly 000 before fixture bytes are opened, while timeout exit 28 fails; docker inspect NetworkMode none and no attachments remain authoritative
runtime_posture.cleanup: remove the run-labeled container with docker rm -fv, then prove no run-labeled container, volume, or network remains; cleanup failure prevents a success receipt

limitations: This is static source and OCI metadata evidence, not a container runtime receipt.
The fixed image has no VISION_INDEX_CLEAN_START switch; freshness depends on the attested tmpfs and zero-count preflight.
The service has no drawing-list endpoint; exact post-index identities are bound by the receipt set plus authoritative count three.

The fixed service has no authentication on index or rebuild routes; network-none plus no host publication makes the verified local-unix Docker daemon the administrative capability boundary for this isolated run. The contract does not defend against a malicious Docker administrator or daemon.

The fixed POST /api/index/add route requires user_name. ER3 pins user_name=review-reuse-er3-fixture and upload_to_s3=false in the exact query string; omitting either fixed argument is a contract failure.
A one-time inspect is insufficient on a shared daemon. Every Docker copy/exec operation must be sealed by before/after normalized inspect projections and bound into the runtime seal receipt.

Index-add creates an in-memory LocalEventBus even with EVENT_BUS_ENABLED=false; EVENT_BUS_USE_LOCAL=true and runtime inspection prevent a Redis path, and explicit rebuild remains required because no index handlers are registered.
The image reports three inconsistent version strings, so only the image digest and source revision identify the substrate.
No image pull, container start, fixture processing, model-quality evaluation, customer-data use, merge, deployment, decision enablement, or pilot is authorized by this attestation.
